title: Compatibility of the Kunneth map with the projection-formula variant
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field, $n\ge1$ invertible in $k$, and let $X$
and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$. Let
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$. Then
the Kunneth map $\kappa_{E,K}$ of
[def-kun-kunneth-map] for the product square is equal to the
composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)\\
&\quad\xrightarrow[\Cref{lem-kun-0f12}]{\ \sim\ }
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}\bigr)\\
&\quad\xrightarrow{\ \RGamma(X_{\Et},\varphi)\ }
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\varphi$ is the map of [lem-kun-0f1n] for the
diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&X&\xleftarrow{\;\pr_1\;}&X\times_kY\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \pr_2}\\
\Spec(k)&\longleftarrow&\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&Y
\end{array}
$$

and the last arrow uses the Leray identification of
[lem-kun-leray-unbdd].

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, $W=X\times_kY$, $p=\pr_1$, $q=\pr_2$, $b:X\to S$, $c:Y\to S$, and $a=b\,p=c\,q$. Write $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $Q=R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K)$, $B=p^{-1}E\otimes^L_\Lambda q^{-1}K$, and $P=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E)$. By [def-kun-separably-closed] we may take $k^{\rm sep}=k$, so its absolute Galois group is trivial. The equivalence [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] and the evaluation formula [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants], with $L=k$, identify abelian sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ with abelian groups by evaluation at $S$. They identify module sheaves with $\Lambda$-modules as well: transport each scalar endomorphism along the fully faithful additive equivalence, and the module identities and linearity of maps are preserved and reflected. Its inverse is the constant-sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. This is an exact equivalence, so termwise application preserves and reflects acyclicity and descends to the unbounded derived categories. Evaluation is already exact, hence needs no further derivation. In the K-injective recipe [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded], evaluation of $Rb_*E$ and $Rc_*K$ is therefore $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Inverse image of the constant complex $Q$ is the constant complex on $X$ by [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. This supplies the identifications in the statement, with coefficient actions retained throughout.

proof.text: Check the finiteness hypotheses for the displayed isomorphisms, without adding separatedness. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X$ and $Y$ admit finite affine covers by finitely generated $k$-algebras. Their pairwise product charts have coordinate rings $A\otimes_k C$, generated by the finite sets $a_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes c_j$; these finitely many charts cover $W$, so $W$ is also finite type over $k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y,W$ Noetherian schemes. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] and [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], each affine chart has Noetherian underlying space. Every open in such a space is quasi-compact: otherwise successively adjoining cover members produces a strictly increasing chain of finite unions of opens. A finite union of these charts has the same property, since an open cover restricts to finite subcovers on each chart. In particular $X$ is quasi-compact and its affine intersections are quasi-compact, so it is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion]. Also $p$ is qcqs: the inverse image of an affine open of $X$ is an open in the Noetherian space $W$, and the inverse image of any affine open under the diagonal of $p$ is again an open in $W$; both are quasi-compact. By [lem-kun-0f10](2), $\operatorname{cd}(X)<\infty$, and by (1), $\operatorname{cd}(p)<\infty$. Since $n\Lambda=0$, [lem-kun-0f12] applies to $(X,E,Q)$, and [lem-kun-leray-unbdd] applies to $(p,B)$. The diagram for [lem-kun-0f1n] has $X'=X$, $S'=S$, $T=Y$, $h=p$, $e=q$, and $g=c$; both squares are cartesian and all schemes are finite type. Its coefficient, invertibility, and unboundedness hypotheses are exactly those here.

proof.text:
Write $\varepsilon_b:b^{-1}P\to E$ and $\varepsilon_c:c^{-1}Q\to K$ for the counits, with the point identifications of step 1 understood. Denote the inverse tensor comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] by $m_u:u^{-1}(L\otimes^L M)\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}L\otimes^L u^{-1}M$. By [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], the first arrow $r$ has adjunct
$$\rho:b^{-1}(P\otimes^L Q)\xrightarrow{m_b}b^{-1}P\otimes^L b^{-1}Q\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_b\otimes1}E\otimes^L b^{-1}Q.$$
Indeed the constant functor in that definition is $b^{-1}$ under step 1, and its counit is $\varepsilon_b$: the sheaf-level adjunction on either side sends a constant section to that section, and the derived adjunction is the termwise Hom bijection on a K-injective resolution, as specified in [def-kun-kunneth-map]. Thus no arbitrary choice of adjunction is being substituted.

Let $V=q^{-1}K$ and $C=b^{-1}Rc_*K=b^{-1}Q$. The defining adjunct of $\xi$ in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is
$$\delta:p^{-1}C\cong q^{-1}c^{-1}Rc_*K\xrightarrow{q^{-1}\varepsilon_c}V.$$
Put $\tau=Rp_*\sigma\circ\mathrm{PF}_p(V,E)\circ\sigma$, and read the canonical map of [lem-kun-0f1n] for this diagram, built as the blueprint proof says from the exchange morphism of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] followed by the projection-formula map, as $\varphi=\tau\circ(1_E\otimes\xi)$. The tensor comparison commutes with symmetry: on a pure tensor in bidegree $(i,j)$ both orders swap the two pulled-back factors and multiply by $(-1)^{ij}$; the K-flat descent justification is given in step 6. Expanding [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and moving the two symmetries past the counit by naturality [lem-kun-tensor-sym], the adjunct of $\tau:E\otimes^L Rp_*V\to Rp_*(p^{-1}E\otimes^L V)$ is $1_{p^{-1}E}\otimes\varepsilon_{p,V}$ after $m_p$. Consequently the adjunct of $\varphi$ is
$$\beta:p^{-1}(E\otimes^L C)\xrightarrow{m_p}p^{-1}E\otimes^L p^{-1}C\xrightarrow{1\otimes p^{-1}\xi}p^{-1}E\otimes^L p^{-1}Rp_*V\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_{p,V}}p^{-1}E\otimes^L V.$$
The last two arrows are $1\otimes\delta$, since $\varepsilon_{p,V}p^{-1}\xi=\delta$ is exactly the adjunction formula defining the exchange mate. Therefore $\beta=(1\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_c)\circ m_p$, with the inverse-image composition maps displayed in $\delta$ included. This is the counit composite whose $p$-adjunct is the canonical map in the counit description of 0F1N (there with $h=p$, $e=q$, $g=c$ and the left map the identity), so the exchange/projection reading and the counit-adjunct reading of $\varphi$ give the same morphism. These are identities of maps for arbitrary unbounded $E,K$; no bounded-below isomorphism theorem has been used.

proof.text: The Leray comparison in the statement composes these very adjunctions. To check its normalization, choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $p_*I$ is K-injective, because the constant-coefficient inverse image is exact (as included in [def-kun-kunneth-map]). Hence both sides of Leray are represented by the same complex $\Gamma(W,I)=\Gamma(X,p_*I)$. In the adjunction Hom bijections specified in [def-kun-kunneth-map], taking the $p$-adjunct and then the $b$-adjunct is the termwise composite-adjunction Hom bijection. The inverse-image composition maps carry the composite units to the single units by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]; thus these Hom bijections agree with the $a$-adjunction. This is the canonical Leray identification of [lem-kun-leray-unbdd], not an unrelated isomorphism of its source and target. Accordingly the $a$-adjunct of $\ell^{-1}R\Gamma(X,\varphi)r$ is $\beta\circ p^{-1}\rho$, with $a^{-1}\cong p^{-1}b^{-1}$ understood.

proof.text:
The canonical tensor and inverse-image composition comparisons used here are compatible: applying a composite pullback to a local tensor $x\otimes y$ and separating its factors gives the same tensor as separating first and pulling back twice. On module sheaves both maps send the pulled-back pair of local generators to that same pair, so they agree by the universal property of tensor and sheafification. For these constant coefficients, module pullback is inverse image: $\Lambda_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\Lambda_V}u^{-1}M\cong u^{-1}M$ by multiplication, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, using [lem-kun-pullback-constant] for the coefficient ring. Since inverse image is exact as recorded in [def-kun-kunneth-map], its derived functor is its termwise functor. Thus the cited ringed-topos pullback result applies to the inverse images here. The generator equality passes to total complexes (degreewise the maps are the same and preserve both differentials and their signs) and then to the derived categories: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] permits K-flat flat-term representatives and their pullbacks, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] says that the resulting natural transformations are determined on those representatives. Thus, by bifunctoriality [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], the composite from step 5 is
$$a^{-1}(P\otimes^L Q)\xrightarrow{m_a}a^{-1}P\otimes^L a^{-1}Q\cong p^{-1}b^{-1}P\otimes^L q^{-1}c^{-1}Q\xrightarrow{p^{-1}\varepsilon_b\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_c}p^{-1}E\otimes^L q^{-1}K.$$
Explicitly, the middle calculation is $(1\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_c)(p^{-1}\varepsilon_b\otimes1)=p^{-1}\varepsilon_b\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_c$; it uses only the bifunctor composition law for tensor, with no factor interchange or extra sign.

proof.text: By [def-kun-kunneth-map], the map displayed in step 6 is exactly $\alpha_{E,K}$, the defining adjunct of $\kappa_{E,K}$, including the tensor comparison and the two inverse-image composition isomorphisms. The two morphisms in the statement consequently have equal images under the same adjunction Hom bijection. Applying its inverse proves $\kappa_{E,K}=\ell^{-1}R\Gamma(X,\varphi)r$, as claimed.

No new nodes and no Lean changes.
split_report.blueprint: Master proof paragraph 1 is step 1 and the normalization in step 3; paragraph 2 is steps 2–6, including the explicit exchange/projection and Leray computations; paragraph 3 is step 7. The current main-20261015 node has the same statement but no proof. No route change.

tool_uses.why: The generic field-point sheaf/Galois equivalence identifies the separably closed base topos with modules; the cited 03QU node only states cohomology vanishing and does not give this equivalence.
The field-point evaluation formula fixes the global-sections normalization of that equivalence; no statement in this unit provides it.
The generic exact-adjoint theorem checks the normalization of the unbounded composition on K-injective representatives; it does not replace the Kunneth route.
Module-linear composition and its compatibility with adjunction units ensure that the composed adjunct is the canonical a-adjunct, not one transported through arbitrary isomorphisms.
The generic K-flat pullback theorem supplies flat-term representatives and preservation for the elementary local-generator check of tensor/composition coherence.
Uniqueness of natural transformations on K-flat flat-term representatives transfers the explicit generator identity to the unbounded derived tensor.

lean.statement:
lemma kunnethMap_eq (p : W ⟶ X) (q : W ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (c : W ⟶ S)
    (hp : p ≫ f = c) (hq : q ≫ g = c)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology A)) :
    kunnethMap A p q f g c hp hq E K =
      ((rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap A f).app E).app (R((g)_*[A]).obj K) ≫
        R((f)_*[A]).map (tensorBaseChangeMap A p q f g (hp.trans hq.symm) E K) ≫
          (rightDerivedLowerStarCompIsoOfComp A p f c hp).hom.app _
lean.note: Existing published theorem, explicitly tagged lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n, read using scompile.py --source. Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u+1} (ULift.{u+1} (ZMod n)), S to Spec k, W to the product, p and q to its projections, f and g to its structure maps, c to p ≫ f, hp to rfl and hq to pullback.condition.symm. Its right side is the canonical projection map, derived pushforward of tensorBaseChangeMap, and canonical composition isomorphism. Through the canonical separably closed point equivalence and Leray, these are exactly the displayed constant-complex projection map, RΓ(X,φ), and last Leray identification, with the same counit normalization. The recorded kunnethGlobalSectionsMap is precisely the canonical transport of the left side. This existing theorem proves the identity for arbitrary schemes and coefficients, hence applies to all the stated finite-type schemes and positive invertible n without extra hypotheses. No new construction or duplicate theorem.
